recipes.name: Parsley and Parmesan Crusted Pork Tenderloin

steps.text: Preheat the oven to 375 degrees F (190 degrees C). Grease a baking dish with cooking spray.
Arrange pork tenderloins in the prepared baking dish.
Mix together bread crumbs, parsley, Parmesan cheese, thyme, salt, and black pepper in a medium bowl until well combined; set aside.
Stir together mustard and garlic in a small bowl until well combined, then spread over pork. Sprinkle bread crumb mixture over mustard coating.

Bake pork in the preheated oven until no longer pink in the center, about 20 minutes. An instant-read thermometer inserted into the center should read 160 degrees F (70 degrees C). Allow pork to rest for 5 minutes before slicing.

raw_recipe.headline: Parsley and Parmesan Crusted Pork Tenderloin
raw_recipe.description: This pork tenderloin features a crust of parsley, Parmesan, thyme, and bread crumbs. It bakes in just 20 minutes and is perfect for your next dinner party.

review.reviewBody: If you’re simply going to top the tenderloin with the crumb mixture you can easily get by with just half of what’s called for. Once I mixed it up and realized I had way more than I needed, a side of me said to simply bag the rest and use it another time (it would have been great on shrimp!). But what I ended up doing was to coat the entire tenderloin with the mustard/garlic mixture, then completely cover it in the bread crumb mixture and drizzled a little olive oil over the top. To prevent it from getting soggy on the bottom, I roasted it on a rack I placed on a cookie sheet. My tenderloin was almost exactly a pound, and it cooked to perfect tender and juicy perfection at 425 degrees for 25 minutes. This is one of the better pork tenderloin recipes I’ve tried, uniquely flavorful with elegant, company-worthy presentation. I used fresh thyme, using the rule of thumb three times as much as dried. I served this with Oven-Roasted Potatoes and Savory Summer Squash, both recipes also from this site.

Like everyone else, I needed to cook it longer. 35 minutes for me. It was tasty and easy! 
I did replace the breadcrumbs with crushed up parmesan crisps to make it more keto friendly.. I also used all the breadcrumb mixture and cooked it on a cookie sheet, as someone suggested.
I think the crust mix would work well with other meats as well.

It was good. Used almond flour rather than panko to keep it wheat free. Also cooked for 30 min to 145 degrees, then let it rest and it was beautifully pink and juicy inside. We really quite enjoyed it!

My family really enjoyed this recipe. The only change I made to the recipe was to pat the bread crumb mixture on all sides of the meat, not just sprinkle the top. 

Also, the recipe says to cook the tenderloin to an internal temperature of 160F. Since 2011, the FDA has said that whole cuts of pork are safe at an internal temperature of 145F. (Ground pork still needs to be cooked to 160F.)

Cooking to an internal temperature of 145F yields a more tender and juicy result. The meat may be slightly pink at 145F, but it's safe. Use a good digital thermometer to be sure.

Our whole family (including a 10 year old boy) loved this! I made a few substitutions - cilantro instead of parsley & fresh thyme instead of dried and used a food processor to make the bread crumbs and get the Parmesan and herbs down to a small size. We followed the new guidelines of 145 degrees and there were no leftovers!

This was delicious! I took another reviewers advice and put the crumb mixture all over. I cooked mine at 400° because I had a maple acorn squash cooking at the same time. I added broccoli to the sheet pan with the acorn squash when I put the meat in. I tossed my broccoli with lemon juice and parm out of the oven. Next time I’ll put it on a rack to cook. My husband said, “This is our next company dinner menu.”

Definitely needs about 45 mins to cook. Definitely use a meat thermometer. I increased oven temp to 425 after 40 mins and let brown for 5-6 mins. Rested about 15 mins. 
I thought it was fabulous and insanely easy. The meat was buttery tender and very tasty. Guests seemed as pleased as I was. I will make it often. Chopping the parsley was the only work! Recipe says this is for 4 servings. It feeds 6 or more. PS. I had leftover coating( parsley, part and crumbs). I threw this in with hot , cooked noodles and some butter. First course was a a large salad with asparagus, pears and pecans.

I used a 24 oz pork loin and increased the cook time to 40 minutes. Covered with foil at 25 minutes to keep the topping from browning too much. Comments from friends was best tasting pork loin they’ve ever had. This one is a definite keeper.

I make this all the time. Delicious. The one thing I do different is to pour a little oil over the breadcrumb/parm cheese and top with balsamic glaze and cook at 400 degrees for 15 minutes then turn oven off for another 15 minutes. Slice and add a little more glaze. Soooo yummy. I use Rachel Rays balsamic glaze

I have made this several times and each time my guests rave about it. I made it the last time and served this cold. It is great either hot or cold. I use all the ingredients and cover the filet all around with mustard I brush on and place it into the bread crumb mixture and roll it till covered. Then I place it on a rack to go into the oven. There is enough bread crumbs mixture to cover three filets fully. I do not use Panko as it is too big I feel. Regular bread crumbs are perfect. I cook in the oven on 425F for 20 minutes then reduce the temperature to 325F to finish for another 15 minutes. I like the pork tenderloin to be a slightly pink color which you can get if you take it out of the oven at 160F .

This is one of the best recipes I've found for Pork Tenderloin. Tender and moist. I followed recipe with only a few adjustments after reading other reviews.
Covered the entire tenderloin in the mustard/breadcrumb mixture. Placed on raised baking rack so the bottom would not be soggy.
Baked 2.24 lb. tenderloin, in 375 degree convection oven, for 40 minutes.
Served with Lemon-spinach orzo, and english peas. 
This is an easy weeknight meal or elegant enough to serve guests

I wish I would have re-read the reviews before I started this. A had a single, 1.5lb pork tenderloin. You need half the breadcrumbs- even if I would have had two 12oz loins. Bake time is also off. Cooked closer to 35-45 min to get to temp. Sprayed with Pam halfway through so that it would start to “crust” better. I really like Dijon but the flavor was just okay. Served with garlic mashed cauliflower from this site - which I think paired nicely. Overall, okay-good. Still glad I tried. Thanks Leanne Cooke!

I used Garlic Powder in my crumbing and we had about a kg of tender loin. So I went off the 4x recipe but used common sense. Such as a cup of parsley and not 2. 3/4 C of mustard and 1T and a t of minced garlic. It worked out perfectly and my family is asking for it even more.
I’ve made this several times and it always turns out well. Follow the recipe and you’ll be fine. Probably one of the easiest tenderloin recipes you’ll find.

It doesn't get much easier than this, when in doubt roast it out. I served with steamed green beans.
Trying to determine why the rub turned out so salty as I followed the recipe exactly. But I cannot say it was under seasoned at all, just a little bit too salty for us and we love salt!
loved the recipe but had not saved it last week. Did no changes to it and served salad, new potatoes and zuccinni. Wanted to make sure to have a hard copy on file.

Outstanding recipe, thank you. I had one 1.2 lb. tenderloin and made 1/2 of the rest of the recipe and had plenty. The aroma as it cooked was incredible. After one bite, the first words out of my husband’s mouth were, “THIS is a keeper!” I used fresh thyme, otherwise followed the recipe and took it out when the temperature reached 150°; after resting in foil it reached 160°.

Great Flavor on this pork. I actually baked it in the grill directly on the top rack. Kept the temperature around 425 for 25-30mins until meat thermometer read 160.
-My changes: Honey Mustard and Minced Garlic--worked great; family loved it.

Think you need to adjust the timing based on your tenderloin size, which was a complaint by a lot of reviewers. This really is a minor issue as long as you have a thermometer or you have experience cooking pork. It took about 45 minutes for me. I used spicy brown mustard and dijon just simply because I ran out of dijon. I would definitely make this again! Even my toddler loved it.
Very good
